question: About how long are the intestines in an adult human body when fully stretched out?
explanation: It sounds unbelievable because they fit inside our belly, but our intestines stretch to about nine meters long! You've got this. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h1)

question: What are the two main sections that the intestinal tract is divided into?
explanation: Nice and simple! The gut is broadly split into the small intestine and the large intestine to handle digestion and waste. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which part of the small intestine connects directly to the stomach?
explanation: The duodenum is that C-shaped first stop where food leaves the stomach and meets up with juices from the liver and pancreas. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h2)

question: A surgeon has to remove the very last section of a patient's small intestine. Which part is this?
explanation: The ileum is the final stretch of the small intestine right before it hands over food waste to the large intestine. Great job remembering that! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h2)

question: What do we call those little pouch-like segments you see along the length of the colon?
explanation: Haustra are the cute little pocket formations on the colon created by its muscle bands. You're building solid anatomy knowledge! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of the large intestine in our daily digestion?

options.A: Producing bile to break down fats

explanation: As food waste travels through, the large intestine pulls out the remaining water, turning liquid into solid stool. Spot on! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which special cells in the lining of the intestine make protective mucus?
explanation: Goblet cells look like little wine goblets and pump out mucus to keep the gut lining slippery and safe from harsh digestive juices. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why does the intestinal wall have a muscular layer (the muscularis)?

options.B: Generating peristaltic waves to move contents
options.C: Filtering waste from local blood vessels
options.D: Absorbing digested sugars and amino acids

explanation: These muscles squeeze in a coordinated wave pattern (peristalsis) to push food smoothly along the digestive tract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h4)

question: Where do water-soluble nutrients go right after they cross the intestinal lining?

options.D: Capillaries leading to the portal vein

explanation: Sugars and amino acids jump straight into the tiny blood capillaries of the villi and head to the liver via the portal vein for processing. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why do intestinal cells have to package dietary fats into structures called chylomicrons?

options.A: To convert fats directly into glucose
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid in the gut
options.C: To allow transport into lymphatic lacteals
options.D: To make the fat molecules taste sweet

explanation: Fats are too bulky to slip directly into blood vessels, so enterocytes package them into chylomicrons so they can travel safely through the lymphatic vessels. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h5)

question: What happens when food moves way too quickly through a person's colon?
explanation: If food rushes through the colon, there's no time to absorb water, leading to loose, watery stools. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does water mostly travel across the lining of the large intestine?

options.D: Being pushed by direct muscular contractions

explanation: Water loves to follow salt! As the gut actively pumps sodium across its lining, water follows it smoothly through osmosis. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which major blood vessel feeds oxygen-rich blood to the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine?
explanation: The superior mesenteric artery is the main lifeline branching off the aorta to supply the small intestine and upper colon. Keep crushing it! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h7)

question: How does your nervous system's 'fight-or-flight' (sympathetic) response affect your intestines?
explanation: When you're stressed or running from danger, your body shuts down non-essentials like digestion to focus energy on surviving. Rest and digest takes a back seat! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h7)

question: What exactly is a paralytic ileus?

options.A: Rapid twisting of the sigmoid colon
options.B: Severe infection of the appendix lining
options.C: Temporary stoppage of intestinal peristalsis after surgery
options.D: A permanent blockage caused by a large tumor

explanation: Sometimes the bowel goes to sleep after abdominal surgery and temporarily stops moving. It's a common post-op watch-out for nurses! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h8)

question: Your patient just came back from abdominal surgery. Their tummy feels a bit swollen and you can't hear any bowel sounds. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong laxative orally right away
options.B: Massage the abdomen vigorously to force gas out
options.C: Encourage the patient to eat a large solid meal
options.D: Keep the patient NPO until bowel activity returns

explanation: If the bowel isn't moving (paralytic ileus), giving food or drink will only cause nausea and vomiting. Keeping them NPO (nothing by mouth) keeps them safe until peristalsis wakes up! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h8)
